newsitem.title: USA: Stocks edge lower, dollar rallies.
newsitem.headline: Stocks edge lower, dollar rallies.

text.p: Stocks edged lower but managed to stay above the 6,000 level on the Dow Jones industrial average Tuesday, while the dollar rallied against most major currencies.
Oil prices fell. Bonds ended little changed.
The Dow Jones industrial fell 5.22 points at 6,004.78, the day after it closed above 6,000 for the first time.

The Nasdaq composite index, laced with high-technology issues, hit a record for the second consecutive day, rising 1.74 points to 1,258.10 as the shares of computer chip maker Intel Corp. surged on a 40 percent jump in third-quarter profits.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,301 to 1,058 on heavy volume of 458 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We've come a long way in a short time ... The odds favour a pause to refresh and then work higher," said Alfred Goldman, technical research director of A.G. Edwards. He noted the market, as measured by the Dow, has risen about 450 points in five weeks and 850 since July 16.
The market's recent gains were fuelled by the outlook for continued moderate economic growth and low inflation, which should help corporate earnings.
Analysts said stocks were searching for a catalyst before making further inroads into record ground.

"The market is tired and needs another catalyst to get it over," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist of Fahnestock & Co. "It could be delivered by CPI but I'm not certain the number has been somewhat discounted."
The Consumer Price Index for September is due on Wednesday, with economists expecting an increase of 0.3 percent, compared with a 0.1 percent rise in the prior month.
Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said stocks were closely tracking the ongoing flood of corporate earnings reports.
In currency markets, the dollar rose to a 33-month high against the Japanese yen and a 20-week high against the German mark, riding the continued strength of the British pound, dealers said.
A rise in the pound tends to aid the dollar as investment flows out of other currencies in Japan and Europe, dealers said.
The dollar touched a high of 112.39 yen, up from Monday's close of 111.66, before ending at 112.25.
The dollar closed at 1.5408 marks after touching a 1.5412 mark high. It closed Monday at 1.5290 marks.
Dealers also cited pent-up demand for dollars after the U.S. currency spent the last several sessions in a narrow trading range.
The key 30-year Treasury bond rose 1/32, or 31.25 cents on a $1,000 bond, lowering its yield to 6.84 percent from 6.85 percent late on Monday.
Oil prices took a breather depite more news of Mideast turmoil, but most traders doubted the rally was over.
Crude oil for November delivery fell 20 cents to $25.42 a barrel at the New York Mercantile Exchange. Overnight, the price had set a post-Gulf War high of $25.72 on NYMEX's electronic trading system.
Overseas, British stocks set a record, with the FTSE 100 index rising 12.1 points to 4,050.8. Tokyo's Nikkei 225 average jumped 400.68 points to close at 21,429.93.
